projects.title: projects
projects.description: Featured projects by Ember: a native macOS/iOS AI assistant, an AI companion, a native Apple Silicon game port, agent tooling, and real-time speech detection.
projects.introHtml: A curated selection of my most notable work. For the full catalog, see my GitHub.

entries.name: SwiftClaw
entries.tagline: Native AI Assistant for macOS and iOS
entries.descriptionHtml: A SwiftUI + SwiftData assistant that works across a multi-account IMAP/SMTP mail client, calendar, reminders, a local-first Markdown notes vault and curated memory, using models from Azure OpenAI, Neuralwatt or OpenRouter. Note edits wait as approval cards, and gated memory writes can be edited before you accept them. Deep Research plans, searches and fetches sources, writes a cited report, and checks cited claims against stored evidence. Its fetcher withholds any response unless every connection reached a public address, which guards against SSRF and DNS rebinding. Notes search fuses SQLite FTS5 and on-device NLEmbedding vectors with reciprocal rank fusion. About 80k lines of Swift 6 under strict concurrency (MainActor by default, actors for background work), with 1,300+ Swift Testing tests.

entries.name: Project Valerie
entries.tagline: Self-Hosted AI Companion with Receipt-Backed Outcomes
entries.descriptionHtml: A single-user AI companion on Telegram, run from a React dashboard. Every turn pins an immutable snapshot of prompts, settings and history that retries reuse, and every tool outcome is recorded as a receipt. Telegram deliveries and image renders count as done only after the external system confirms them. Includes revisioned prompts, long-term memory with Obsidian vault retrieval, time-zone-exact reminders, bounded tool calls and ComfyUI image generation. A Bun workspace monorepo with ~60k lines of strict TypeScript, SQLite with no ORM, 500+ tests in CI, and backend hot-reload that keeps the database and Telegram polling alive.

entries.name: pf-wotr-silicon
entries.tagline: Native Apple Silicon Port of a Shipped Unity Game
entries.descriptionHtml: Build tooling that turns a Steam install of Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous (Intel-only on Mac) into a native arm64 build without touching the original. Includes a C++ shim that implements the legacy Steamworks 1.41 API on a modern universal library, and a mod that replaces a slow managed DXT texture compressor with a native one, verified byte-identical across ~9.3M fuzzed blocks. Measured on an M2 Max against the Rosetta build: first-play cutscene hitches drop from ~36 to ~5 and p99 frame time from 34 ms to 22 ms. The native compressor plus shorter cleanup waits cut save loads from ~11.5 s to ~6.5 s.

entries.name: HarnessDeck
entries.tagline: Local Control Center for Claude Code and Codex
entries.descriptionHtml: A local web dashboard for coding agents. It runs persistent agent sessions in tmux, streamed to xterm.js over WebSockets, and adds structured chats with git worktree isolation, a skills manager that syncs between harnesses, and usage tracking. Harnesses sit behind a common driver interface, and Codex is integrated through its typed app-server protocol. Since the server can start real shells, every request must carry an allowed loopback or tailnet Host, and any browser Origin must match it. That blocks cross-site and DNS-rebinding attacks.

entries.name: Swear Jar
entries.tagline: Real-Time Speech Detection + Live Stream Widget
entries.descriptionHtml: Two-part system for live streams. Vox, a Python TUI built on Textual and faster-whisper, captures audio, transcribes it and detects profanity. It sends events to an authenticated Bun service, which broadcasts them over WebSockets to an animated OBS browser-source widget. The web service is deployable with Docker.
